title: Knowing You
lyrics_original: All I once held dear, built my life upon
All this world reveres and wars to own;
All I once thought gain I have counted loss,
Spent and worthless now compared to this.
Knowing You, Jesus, knowing You
There is no greater thing
You're my all, You're the best
You're my joy, my righteousness,
And I love You Lord.
Now my heart's desire is to know You more,
To be found in You and known as Yours,
To possess by faith what I could not earn
All surpassing gift of righteousness
Knowing You, Jesus, knowing You
There is no greater thing
You're my all, You're the best
You're my joy, my righteousness,
And I love You Lord.
Oh to know the power of Your risen life,
And to know You in Your sufferings;
To become like You in Your death, my Lord,
So with You to live and never die.
Knowing You, Jesus, knowing You
There is no greater thing
You're my all, You're the best
You're my joy, my righteousness,
And I love You Lord.

bible_verses.english: However, what things were gain to me, these have I counted loss for Christ.

Yes, most certainly, and I count all things to be loss for the excellence of the knowledge of Christ Jesus, my Lord, for whom I suffered the loss of all things, and count them as refuse, that I may gain Christ
Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a treasure hidden in the field, which a man found, and hid. In his joy, he goes and sells all that he has, and buys that field.

devotional.prayer_english: Lord Jesus, thank You for being the greatest treasure of my life. Forgive me for the times I hold tightly to things that cannot satisfy my soul. Open my eyes to see the beauty of knowing You more deeply each day. You are my joy, my righteousness, and my all, and my heart's deepest desire is simply to love You more. Amen.
devotional.prayer_original: Lord Jesus, thank You for being the greatest treasure of my life. Forgive me for the times I hold tightly to things that cannot satisfy my soul. devotional.reflection_english: It is easy to measure our worth by what we accumulate, build, or achieve in this life. Yet, when we catch a glimpse of who Jesus is, everything else naturally pales in comparison. Like finding a priceless treasure in a field, knowing Christ reshapes our desires and redefines what truly matters. Surrendering our earthly gains isn't a tragic sacrifice, but a joyful trade for the ultimate gift—a personal, deep relationship with our Savior who is our joy, righteousness, and all.
